title: Hover returns null for multi-word and in-section commands
description: Hover over stdio (Neovim repro) resolves only single-token keywords via the node kind or first anonymous leaf. It returns null for: (1) generic command_line nodes (ip address, ip access-group, switchport access vlan) because Lookup runs on the bare first token 'ip'; (2) multi-word headers like router_header ('router' misses, DB key is 'router bgp'); (3) negated commands (no ip address). Diagnostics already solves this with firstKeywordFromNode longest-prefix probing; hover needs the same resolution.
close_reason: Hover now resolves command-like nodes via longest-prefix keyword probing (multi-word commands, headers, negated forms); regression + golden tests added

title: Add CI workflow running make test and make cover on push and PR
description:
Testing-gap analysis found there is no .github/workflows/ directory — the test gate only fires at release time via goreleaser before-hooks. Ordinary pushes and PRs run nothing between releases.

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on push and pull_request:
- make test (CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./...; works out of the box on ubuntu-latest, no sibling grammar checkout needed since both targets use the published module)
- make cover (enforces COVER_MIN=75 total floor, currently ~81.3%)

Consider also running the job matrix or at least one darwin runner if darwin-specific behavior matters, but linux amd64 alone is sufficient to start. Keep it minimal: no release automation, just the gate.
acceptance_criteria: GitHub Actions workflow file committed that runs make test and make cover on push and pull_request and passes on the repo's default branch.
close_reason: CI workflow added: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs make test + make cover on push/PR. PR #1

title: Add end-to-end JSON-RPC wire test driving chunt serve like an editor
description:
Testing-gap analysis found that internal/protocol (all LSP DTOs) has zero tests and cmd/serve.go's jrpc2 wiring (channel framing, assigner mapping, push channel) is untested. server_test.go calls methods directly on server.Server via a stub feature, bypassing JSON-RPC serialization — a bad struct tag in protocol would pass every existing test but break every editor client.

Add an integration test that spins up the jrpc2 server over an in-memory pipe (or spawns the built bin/chunt) and scripts a full editor session:
- initialize → initialized handshake, verify returned capabilities and serverInfo
- textDocument/didOpen → assert publishDiagnostics notification arrives with expected payloads
- textDocument/didChange → assert diagnostics update
- Real completion/hover/definition/references/documentSymbol requests against a fixture .ios.j2 with known content, asserting response shape and content
- shutdown → exit, clean server termination

This closes the biggest reliability gap (protocol marshaling + assigner + framing) and covers internal/protocol and cmd/serve.go indirectly. Consider building it as a reusable harness so other protocol-level tests can share it (see linked edge-case issue).
acceptance_criteria: go test passes with a full wire-level session covering initialize/didOpen/didChange/feature requests/shutdown/exit; publishDiagnostics push verified; protocol package covered indirectly; no changes to production code required to make the test pass (or minimal, justified ones).
close_reason: Wire harness in internal/server/wire_test.go: full editor session over real jrpc2 channel incl. publishDiagnostics push; also fixed DidChange stale-tree bug. PR #3

title: Normalize CRLF line endings in the document layer (diagnostic ranges shift on CRLF input)
description:
Discovered while bringing up the windows-latest CI job (v0.15.0 windows release): when a document contains CRLF line endings, tree-sitter diagnostic ranges shift. Example from the golden harness: a missing-`\}\}` ERROR node reports 0:12-12 on LF input but 0:12-13 on CRLF input, because the CR is absorbed into the error region; every golden comparison also breaks. CI checkout determinism was fixed separately via .gitattributes pinning *.cfg/*.marks/*.golden to LF (commit c5052f9), but this is a RUNTIME issue: any client that sends CRLF document content — the common case for Windows editors saving .ios.j2 files — gets slightly-off ranges on every platform, not just Windows.

Scope:
- Normalize line endings (CRLF -> LF) in chunt's document layer before parsing, and translate positions back if the editor's buffer is CRLF (LSP positions are per-line, so a trailing CR only affects end-of-line columns — verify hover/completion/definition/references mapping against a CRLF buffer too).
- Add a golden fixture with CRLF content covering diagnostics + at least one position-based feature.
- Keep raw byte offsets consistent with what the LSP client expects for the original buffer.

title: Extend golden harness marks to definition, references, and documentSymbol
description:
Testing-gap analysis found that TestGolden's readMarks switch only supports completion and hover marks (anything else is a fatal 'unknown mark feature'). Definition, References, and DocumentSymbol therefore never run through the full-pipeline golden tier — they only have inline unit tests, so cross-feature interactions (e.g. definition resolving in a file with duplicate definitions) have no full-pipeline regression protection.

Extend golden_test.go:
- Add 'definition', 'references' (with and without includeDeclaration via note syntax or two mark kinds), and 'documentSymbol' cases to the mark dispatch
- Add formatters for []protocol.Location and []protocol.DocumentSymbol matching the existing deterministic style (sorted, compact range rendering)
- Add marks and regenerate goldens for existing fixtures where the features are interesting (undefined_refs.cfg, duplicates.cfg, clean_all_sections.cfg)

Keep the harness's existing properties: raw .cfg with no inline markers, sorted deterministic output, -update regeneration.
acceptance_criteria: Golden fixtures exercise definition/references/documentSymbol through the full pipeline; go test -run TestGolden passes; goldens regenerated with -update and committed.
close_reason: Golden marks extended: definition/references/references-decl/documentSymbol across fixtures. PR #2

title: Test LSP protocol edge cases over the wire
description:
Testing-gap analysis: server_test.go covers the state machine (shutdown-before-initialize etc.) at the direct method-call level, but protocol-level edge cases over the JSON-RPC wire are untested:
- exit notification without prior shutdown
- requests arriving before initialize (spec says the server should error with ServerNotInitialized, -32602 family)
- unknown methods / notifications (should not crash; jrpc2 default behavior may need verification)
- didOpen/didChange for unknown or closed documents over the wire
- malformed JSON-RPC payload handling

Builds on the end-to-end wire harness from the linked issue — implement these as additional scripted sessions against that harness.

Testing-gap analysis discovered the underlying gap.
acceptance_criteria: Wire-level tests exist for each edge case above; behavior matches the LSP spec where it specifies one (or a documented, deliberate deviation); suite green under -race.
close_reason: 8 wire-edge tests + stateGate assigner (-32002/-32600 fixes); branch wt/chunt-ded pushed, PR after l8q merges

title: Add fuzz targets for parse, index, and diagnostics pipeline
description:
Testing-gap analysis: chunt's pipeline is a parser front-end (tree-sitter CGO) plus custom heuristics over arbitrary user input. A panic anywhere in symbols.Index, runDiagnostics, Completion/Hover/Definition/References, or the keyword/section resolution would take down the whole LSP server for the editor session. The current suite is table-driven and never feeds adversarial input.

Add Go fuzz targets, e.g.:
- FuzzDiagnostics: arbitrary string → parse → symbols.Index → all diagnostic passes, assert no panic
- FuzzCursorFeatures: parse valid-ish input, call Completion/Hover/Definition/References at every line:col within bounds (or sampled), assert no panic and positions are in range
- Seed corpus from existing fixtures (testdata/golden/*.cfg) and known-bug corpus cases

Run as regular tests in CI (short mode, seed corpus only) so make test covers them; fuzzing proper is on-demand (go test -fuzz).
acceptance_criteria: Fuzz targets committed with seeded corpus; make test runs the seed corpus without failure; at least one 60s ad-hoc fuzz run per target completed locally without finding a crash (or found crashes fixed).
close_reason: FuzzDiagnostics + FuzzCursorFeatures with seeded corpus; 60s runs clean. PR #4
